successCriteria.description: The LeaveType domain model is exported from the leave-policy module and its `code` field is typed as the LeaveTypeCode enum imported from the shared-types barrel (annual/sick/emergency/unpaid/maternity/paternity), not a raw string.

The repository interface declares all six operations — findAll, findById, findByCode, create, update, delete — and the concrete repository class implements that interface (TypeScript structural/`implements` satisfaction), so the interface can be used as the injection contract.

repository.create persists a new leave_types row via a parameterized INSERT and returns the persisted LeaveType (with server-generated id/timestamps), defaulting isActive to true when omitted and storing description as null when omitted.

repository.update applies only the fields present in the DTO via a dynamically-built parameterized UPDATE, refreshes updated_at, returns the updated LeaveType when a row matched, and returns null when no row matched the id.

repository.findById and findByCode return null (not throw) when no row matches; findAll returns an empty array when the table has no rows; delete returns a boolean indicating whether a row was removed.
The leave-policy barrel (index.ts) re-exports LeaveType, the repository interface, the concrete repository class, and both DTOs, so downstream modules import only through the barrel.

Jest unit tests in tests/unit/modules/leave-policy/ cover the repository with a mocked pg pool, asserting the SQL/parameters issued and the mapped return values for each operation including the not-found and empty cases.

constraints: No ORM — the repository must issue SQL through the pg Pool directly with parameterized queries ($1, $2, …); values are passed as bind parameters, never string-interpolated into the SQL text.

No use of `any` (HARNESS no-any rule): parameter/value arrays must use `unknown[]` with type guards, and the row-to-domain mapping must cast the DB `code` string to LeaveTypeCode rather than leaving it untyped.

All database access is encapsulated inside the repository class (GP-001 / no-direct-db-outside-repository); services and other modules must not import pg or issue SQL — they consume the repository through its interface.
Modules import from each other only through their declared public barrel (index.ts); the leave-policy module imports LeaveTypeCode via the shared-types barrel, not from the enum file's internal path.

The repository must accept an injectable query-capable client (constructor-injected, defaulting to the shared pool) so a service can pass a transaction client for atomic units of work, per the Transaction Contract.
outOfScope: LeavePolicy model, repository, service, and routes (Phase 3 and Phase 8) — this phase owns only the LeaveType catalog entity and its repository within the leave-policy module.
HTTP routes, controllers, RBAC guards, and request validation for leave-type CRUD — no API surface is built in this phase; the repository is consumed programmatically only.

Audit record writing for LeaveType create/update/delete (GP-002) — audit integration is deferred; this phase's repository does not emit audit records. (Note: GP-002 applies to state-changing operations at the service/API layer, which does not yet exist for leave-policy.)
Database migrations / schema creation for the leave_types table — the repository assumes the table exists per the reconciled schema; DDL is out of scope for this phase.

Soft-delete vs hard-delete semantics beyond the current boolean-returning delete — lifecycle deactivation via isActive is supported by update, but a separate soft-delete column or restore flow is not introduced.

ambiguities.description: The repository's `delete` issues a hard DELETE. The reconciled architecture describes LeaveType lifecycle as ACTIVE/INACTIVE (deactivation via isActive), and LeavePolicy/LeaveRequest hold foreign keys to leave_types. A hard delete could break referential integrity if historical rows reference the type. It is unclear whether delete should be permitted at all, or whether it is intended only for never-used catalog entries.
options: Keep hard DELETE as-is (acceptable only for unreferenced rows; rely on DB FK constraints to reject deletes that would orphan rows)
Replace delete with a soft-deactivate (set isActive=false) and drop the hard-delete operation
Keep both: hard delete for unreferenced rows plus isActive toggle for lifecycle

entityInvariants.invariant: A LeaveType's `code` must be one of the six LeaveTypeCode enum values (annual, sick, emergency, unpaid, maternity, paternity); the DB column is unique per the reconciled schema, so no two LeaveType rows may share the same code.

LeaveType has an ACTIVE/INACTIVE lifecycle expressed via the isActive flag; deactivation (isActive=false) is reversible and does not delete the row, preserving referential integrity for historical LeavePolicy and LeaveRequest rows.
createdAt and updatedAt are server-managed timestamps (set on insert, refreshed on every update); the repository must never accept or persist caller-supplied timestamps for these fields.

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns LeaveType[] (empty array when none); never returns null. Throws only on DB/connection failure.
Returns LeaveType | null — null when no row matches the id/code, never throws for not-found. Throws only on DB/connection failure.

Returns the persisted LeaveType with server-generated id and timestamps. A duplicate code violates the unique constraint and surfaces as a DB error (caller maps to a typed error); the repository does not swallow it.

Returns LeaveType | null — null when no row matched the id (idempotent no-op on missing entity). When the DTO carries no fields, returns the current row without issuing an UPDATE. Throws only on DB/connection failure.
Returns boolean — true when a row was removed, false when no row matched. Throws only on DB/connection failure.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The LeaveType model's `code` field and the repository's create/update DTO `code` field must be typed as the LeaveTypeCode enum exported from this file (via the shared-types barrel), matching the six members annual/sick/emergency/unpaid/maternity/paternity exactly — no extra members, no string alias.

The leave_types table columns the repository queries must match the reconciled conceptual data model: id, code, label, description, is_active, created_at, updated_at — with `code` carrying a unique index. The row-to-domain mapping must translate snake_case DB columns to the camelCase LeaveType interface and convert null description to undefined.

The repository must obtain its default database connection from the shared pg Pool exported here, and must not instantiate its own Pool; transaction participation is via the injectable client abstraction, not a second pool.

The module boundary and dependency map must hold: leave-policy depends only on shared-types (and audit, reserved for later phases); the leave-policy barrel is the sole public entry point, and no internal file is imported directly by other modules.

integrationPoints.why: The LeaveType model and repository DTOs depend on the LeaveTypeCode type from Phase 1; this is the hard cross-module dependency and the only shared type consumed in this phase.
The repository's default query execution target; all SQL flows through this pool (or an injected transaction client sharing its query shape).
Downstream phases (LeavePolicy repository in Phase 3, LeavePolicyService in Phase 8, and leave-request/balance modules) consume LeaveType and ILeaveTypeRepository exclusively through this barrel.
